name: John J. O'Connor
description: Architect of Saint Paul's famed 'O'Connor system.' Formulated the informal municipal policy offering safe harbor to criminals provided they registered, paid fees, and committed no major crimes within city limits.
qualifications: Synthesized from historical accounts; no signed personal policy document survives.

name: William 'Reddy' Griffin
description: Served as the initial intermediary between Chief O'Connor and out-of-town criminals, handling check-ins and tribute until his death in 1913.
qualifications: Attributed to MNHS historical overview of underworld broker succession.

name: Dan 'Dapper Dan' Hogan
role: Proprietor of the Green Lantern Saloon and underworld broker
description: Succeeded Griffin as chief fixer in Saint Paul. Operates the Green Lantern on Wabasha Street as a clearinghouse for information, bond bailouts, and underworld diplomacy. Killed by an early automotive car bomb in 1928.
qualifications: The 1928 bombing remains legally unsolved; no assailant was ever convicted.

name: Leon Gleckman
aliases: The Al Capone of Saint Paul
role: Bootlegging syndicate leader and political powerbroker
description: Maintained an executive suite at the Saint Paul Hotel, wielding substantial influence over local police appointments and ward politics. Prosecuted federally for tax evasion and jury tampering.
qualifications: Court opinions document tax fraud and juror contempt; do not substantiate generalized rumors of absolute political control.

name: Bernard Fuchs
role: Juror in the 1934 Gleckman federal tax trial
description: Held out against guilty verdicts in Gleckman's first trial, causing a mistrial. Subsequent appellate decisions confirmed he accepted a $300 bribe and pressured credit loans arranged by Gleckman.
qualifications: Adjudicated by the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals under criminal contempt proceedings.

name: William Hamm Jr.
role: President of the Theo. Hamm Brewing Company; victim
description: Abducted outside his residence on June 15, 1933 by the Barker-Karpis gang. Held in Wisconsin until a $100,000 ransom was delivered, marking the collapse of the city's immunity guarantee for prominent residents.
qualifications: Kidnapping occurred at the residence on Cable Street rather than the commercial brewery.

name: Edward G. Bremer
role: President of Commercial State Bank; victim
description: Ambushed and abducted at Lexington and Goodrich after dropping his daughter at school. Subjected to three weeks of captivity and coerced messages until a $200,000 ransom was paid.
qualifications: Historical date established as January 17, 1934; earlier printing errors corrected.

name: Walter W. Magee
role: Saint Paul contractor and Bremer family friend; intermediary
description: Targeted by kidnappers to receive ransom communications and act as courier under threat of Bremer's execution. Coordinated with federal and municipal law enforcement despite warnings.
qualifications: Documented in federal investigation summaries; actions were constrained by severe coercion.

name: Harry Sawyer
role: Underworld finger man and Barker-Karpis associate
description: Operated a roadhouse north of Saint Paul. Investigators identified him as selecting Bremer as an extortion target rather than attempting a high-risk bank vault heist.
qualifications: Attributed to FBI post-investigation summary reports; not contemporaneous planning wiretaps.

name: John Dillinger
description: Rented an apartment at Lincoln Court under an assumed name after escaping crown custody. Detected by building management, engaged in a shootout with local police and federal agents on March 31, 1934, escaping wounded.
qualifications: Attendance at Castle Royal remains disputed; presence at Lincoln Court is documented by eyewitness and agent records.

name: Evelyn 'Billie' Frechette
description: Lived with Dillinger at Lincoln Court. Arrested in Chicago in April 1934 and tried in Saint Paul's Landmark Center federal courtroom, convicted of conspiracy to harbor a fugitive and sentenced to two years in prison.
qualifications: Conviction was specifically for harboring a federal fugitive, not participating in bank robberies.

name: Homer Van Meter
description: Arrived at Lincoln Court on March 31 during surveillance, encountered agents in the lobby stairs, and initiated gunfire that facilitated Dillinger and Frechette's escape.
qualifications: Agency sequence reconstructed from conflicting officer and witness statements.
